summary: The doc's 'Adding or removing a rule on that mechanism still works' claim was unconditional in the original PR text, but false whenever the stall lands on one of the #4999 residual sites (arm()/disarm() still block there). docs-writer deferred sizing to a domain agent per governance rule 3; cpp-safety/consistency-auditor/enterprise-readiness each independently confirmed the underlying fact via direct source read. severity_native disagreement recorded: enterprise-readiness's own SHOULD label is a native label: the derived band, per the E6 cap rule (wrong outcome proven unable to occur in production today, since prefer_spark_ defaults false), is LOW; the derived band governs the gate per the shared preamble.
classification_rationale: Doc statement contradicted the actual code (residual under-mu_ sites) as it stood at PR-open; corrected in this PR's fix rounds (f39755e0d, 3a2fea5c7).

trigger: a maintainer reads log_pass_outcome()'s doc comment to understand why the noexcept/catch(...) wrapper exists
summary: The first fix-round's new doc comment overstated the throw-risk mechanism (claimed a single fmt-allocation failure would be thread death; spdlog's own SPDLOG_TRY/CATCH already catches that internally). Round-2 Gate 8 re-review then found the CORRECTED wording itself carried two further, mutually-differing mechanism inaccuracies (a missed non-std::exception rethrow path per cpp-expert; an inaccurate 'rate-limited' custom-handler claim per security-guardian). Round-3 (commit 3a2fea5c7) deliberately simplified the comment to state only the load-bearing, verifiable fact without asserting the specific internal mechanism, closing the round-over-round nitpicking; security-guardian's final round-2-of-gate-8 pass verified the simplified wording against spdlog 1.17.0's actual source and confirmed it is now defensible for both failure shapes.
classification_rationale: An in-code comment asserting a specific mechanism that turned out to be inaccurate is a truth finding per governance rule 3's exception (adjacent to a resource-safety rationale, not mere wording), owned by the domain agent (cpp-safety/security-guardian), not docs-writer.

classification_rationale: A tracking artifact (not a doc required by the six-item list) going stale as a side effect of this PR's own line insertions, twice; corrected by commenting on the issue directly, outside this PR's diff.
